title: IFC from the inside
sub: The building tree, properties and GlobalId
cards/0/body:
IFC (Industry Foundation Classes) is maintained by buildingSMART and is the ISO 16739 standard.

The most common versions are IFC2x3 and IFC4. IFC4.3 added infrastructure: roads, bridges, railways.
cards/1/body:
Everything sits in a spatial structure: IfcProject → IfcSite → IfcBuilding → IfcBuildingStorey (a floor) → elements: IfcWall, IfcDoor, IfcWindow, IfcSlab.

Properties are grouped into property sets. For example, Pset_WallCommon: FireRating, IsExternal, LoadBearing.
cards/2/task: Filter for the doors on the second floor.
cards/3/q: How many doors are on the second floor?
cards/3/explain: Two interior doors and one to the balcony.
cards/4/task: Find all walls that have a fire rating set, and open the properties of one of them.
cards/5/q: Arrange the IFC spatial structure from top to bottom
cards/6/body: The most common IFC encoding is the same ISO 10303-21 text format used by STEP in mechanical engineering: numbered lines that refer to each other.
cards/6/deep: A GlobalId is a 128-bit GUID written as 22 characters in a special base64 alphabet. It is how an object is recognized across model updates and in BCF issues. There are also ifcXML and ifcZIP, and buildingSMART is developing IFC5 with a different, more web-friendly design.
cards/7/q: Which line sets the fire rating?
cards/7/explain: IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE named FireRating with the value REI 90. Line 4 attaches the property set to wall #120.
cards/8/q: What does IFC contain? Select all.
cards/8/explain: IFC is a snapshot for exchange. History and program internals stay in the program’s native file.
cards/9/pairs/3/1: The “element is on this floor” link
